headline: Wildfire smoke exposure in pregnancy linked to asthma in young children
dek: A study of 1,097 full-term children born in Northern California found the asthma risk clustered in the second and third trimesters, according to a summary of work presented at ACAAI 2026.
body:
Exposure to wildfire smoke during pregnancy was linked to asthma in young children, according to a study presented at the 2026 meeting of the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology.

The study included 1,097 full-term children born in Northern California. According to a summary of the findings posted on X, the risk clustered in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy.

Lead author Anh Nguyen said that staying indoors, keeping windows closed and using an air purifier on smoky days can lower how much smoke pregnant women breathe in.

The findings were shared on X on 16 November 2026 by Moms Clean Air Force, a community that describes itself as united against air pollution.
